article.title: SK Hynix reports Q3 revenue up 328% YoY to ~$78.8B, vs. ~$74.07B est., and operating profit up 632% to ~$62.76B, vs. ~$57.78B est.

research.comment: E1 provides the core news: SK Hynix posted YoY revenue +328% and operating profit +632%, beating estimates. The mandate covers semiconductor and electronic components, prioritizing material changes in chip demand, capacity, revenue, margins, and manufacturing technology. The Q3 beat signals extraordinary demand and pricing power in memory, an important chip segment. E2 matches reveal related context: Samsung Electronics reported similarly exceptional Q3 results; an article details how AI hyperscaler demand has quintupled flash memory prices and shifted negotiating power from Apple to memory suppliers. The HBM and flash demand drivers are documented in that E2 excerpt. From company lookups, 8

ideas.thesis: SK Hynix, a memory chipmaker, reported Q3 revenue and operating profit sharply above estimates (E1). The beat, together with the separate report that AI hyperscaler flash demand has quintupled prices (E2), provides a documented potential catalyst tied to sustained memory demand and pricing. SK Hynix's announced over $25B in dividends and buybacks (E1, E2) further signals management confidence.
ideas.risk: The Q3 results and shareholder return program are widely publicized; the stock may already reflect the beat. The press cannot determine when information was priced in.

ideas.thesis: Samsung Electronics (E2 record: Q3 record revenue +127% YoY, record operating profit +783%, roughly in line with estimates) is a major competitor in memory. The same AI-driven flash pricing dynamics documented in E2 apply to Samsung's memory business, providing a thematic catalyst. Samsung could benefit from the secular memory upcycle, though the text does not confirm HBM market share splits.
ideas.risk: Samsung's Q3 results were broadly in line with estimates (E2), so its beat magnitude is less extreme than SK Hynix's and the news may have different pricing dynamics. Earnings were already reported.

memo.criteria: We invest in semiconductors and electronic components across chip designers, foundries, fabrication equipment, memory, advanced packaging and supply chains. Prioritize material changes in chip demand, capacity, revenue, margins, capital spending, manufacturing technology, supply constraints and export restrictions. Both positive and negative developments can create research opportunities. AI or cloud news matters when a concrete connection to chip demand or suppliers is supported. Consumer apps, retail earnings, routine product launches and political stories have low priority without a documented semiconductor transmission. Score the value of researching the news for this mandate, not whether to buy or sell and not its expected return. Distinguish source evidence from speculation and flag limited excerpt coverage.
